newsitem.title: USA: Best Products receives sell-off approval.
newsitem.headline: Best Products receives sell-off approval.

text.p: Best Products Co. Inc. received bankruptcy court approval Tuesday to essentially shut down the 40-year-old retailer, lay off thousands of employees, and hold going-out-of-business sales at its stores.
U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Douglas Tice in Richmond approved selling Best's assets to a group of investors in a deal worth $423 million.
The investment group will conduct the liquidation sales at Best's 88 stores and 11 jewelry-only outlets, beginning Wednesday.
Liquidation sales started last month at 81 other Best stores.
The sales should be completed by late February. At that point, Best will cease to exist as a retailer.
Best filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Sept. 24, 27 months after emerging from the court's protection in its first trip through Chapter 11.
"It was a necessary action to stop the haemorrhaging of losses," said Harvey Miller, the New York lawyer who represents Best in the case.

Best received more for its assets than it was originally offered thanks to a bidding war in the bankruptcy court that raised the stakes. The assets include merchandise, furniture, fixtures and real estate at the chain's stores as well as its corporate offices.
The investment group had agreed to buy Best's assets in a complicated deal for $410 million.
After the 90-minute auction, the investment group won by raising its offer to $423 million.
The group is composed of Jubilee Limited Partnership III, controlled by the Schottenstein family of Columbus, Ohio; Bernstein Financial Group LLC; Alco Capital Group Inc.; and the Nassi Group LLC.
Gordon Brothers Partners Inc, a Boston-based liquidation company, lost in the bidding.
"This is a much better offer that maximizes the value for the benefit of the creditors," said Scott Hazan, a New York attorney who represents Best's creditors.
